vineyards.name: Les Cras

vineyards.name: Les Petits Vougeots

vineyards.name: Aux Brûlées

vineyards.name: Clos des Corvées
vineyards.style_notes: Southern section — structured and mineral

vineyards.name: Les Fichots
vineyards.style_notes: Reliable reds — firm but fruity

vineyards.name: Aux Vergelesses

vineyards.style_notes: Adjacent to Beaune — structured, slightly austere

vineyards.name: Les Narbantons
vineyards.style_notes: Southern exposure — ripe, generous fruit

vineyards.name: Les Dominodes
vineyards.style_notes: Charming, aromatic — approachable young

vineyards.name: Les Teurons

vineyards.name: Les Bressandes
vineyards.style_notes: Elegant and aromatic — one of the most popular Beaune Premier Crus

vineyards.name: Les Marconnets
vineyards.style_notes: Adjacent to Savigny — firm, structured, tannic in youth

vineyards.name: Les Cras
vineyards.style_notes: High on the slope — mineral and taut

vineyards.name: Les Avaux

vineyards.name: Les Épenots
vineyards.style_notes: More elegant than Rugiens — silky with firm backbone

vineyards.name: Les Grands Épenots
vineyards.style_notes: Best part of Épenots — concentrated, complex

vineyards.name: Les Pézerolles
vineyards.style_notes: Adjacent to Beaune — more finesse than typical Pommard

vineyards.name: Clos des Epeneaux

vineyards.name: Les Arvelets
vineyards.style_notes: Higher elevation — lighter but persistent

vineyards.name: Les Jarollières
vineyards.style_notes: Near Volnay border — shows more elegance

communes.name: Volnay

vineyards.name: Clos des Ducs

vineyards.name: Taillepieds
vineyards.style_notes: Structure and elegance — one of the top 3 Premier Crus. Ages magnificently

vineyards.name: Les Caillerets

vineyards.name: Santenots

vineyards.name: Champans
vineyards.style_notes: Full-bodied for Volnay — structured, earthy, serious

vineyards.name: Clos de la Bousse-d'Or
vineyards.style_notes: Monopole of Domaine de la Pousse d'Or — charming, fragrant

vineyards.name: Les Chevrets
vineyards.style_notes: Lower slope — approachable, fruity, ready earlier

vineyards.name: Frémiets
vineyards.style_notes: Adjacent to Pommard — firmer structure than typical Volnay

communes.style_notes: Hidden behind Volnay — similar style at much lower prices. Insider's Burgundy

vineyards.name: Sur la Velle
vineyards.style_notes: Adjacent to Volnay — shows that commune's elegance

vineyards.name: Les Duresses
vineyards.style_notes: Shared with Auxey — firm, structured reds

communes.name: Auxey-Duresses
communes.style_notes: Value commune — good reds and increasingly fine whites. Side valley microclimate

vineyards.name: Les Duresses
vineyards.style_notes: Best site — structured reds with aging potential

vineyards.name: Climat du Val
vineyards.style_notes: Good whites — mineral and fresh

vineyards.name: Les Grands Champs
vineyards.style_notes: Charming reds — lighter style

vineyards.name: Les Genevrières
vineyards.style_notes: Between Perrières and Charmes in style — floral, mineral, complex

vineyards.name: Les Gouttes d'Or

vineyards.name: Le Porusot
vineyards.style_notes: Adjacent to Perrières — similar mineral precision

vineyards.name: Blagny
vineyards.style_notes: Higher elevation — taut, mineral, needs time

vineyards.name: Clos des Perrières
vineyards.style_notes: Monopole of Albert Grivault — within Perrières, walled vineyard. Exceptional

vineyards.name: Les Cras
vineyards.style_notes: Steely and precise — lean style, ages beautifully

vineyards.name: Sous le Dos d'Âne
vineyards.style_notes: Near Blagny — mineral, taut, excellent value

communes.name: Blagny
communes.style_notes: Tiny hamlet between Meursault and Puligny — reds sold as Blagny, whites as Meursault or Puligny Premier Cru

vineyards.name: La Pièce sous le Bois
vineyards.style_notes: Largest Blagny climat — firm, rustic reds

communes.style_notes: Finest white Burgundy — mineral precision, elegance, crystalline purity

vineyards.style_notes: Within Bâtard on the Puligny side — floral, delicate, sometimes the most charming

vineyards.name: Les Folatières

vineyards.name: Les Combettes
vineyards.style_notes: Adjacent to Meursault Charmes — richer, more opulent style for Puligny

vineyards.name: Clavoillon
vineyards.style_notes: Leflaive monopole — pure, fine-boned, mineral

vineyards.name: Les Perrières
vineyards.style_notes: High on the slope — taut, mineral, austere in youth

vineyards.name: Champ Canet
vineyards.style_notes: Above Combettes — generous, round, accessible

vineyards.name: Les Referts
vineyards.style_notes: South of the village — charming, ready earlier

vineyards.name: Clos de la Garenne
vineyards.style_notes: Within Les Folatières — Duc de Magenta monopole. Concentrated

communes.name: Chassagne-Montrachet
communes.style_notes: Rich white Burgundy and underrated reds — more generous than Puligny

vineyards.name: Montrachet (Chassagne portion)

communes.name: Bonnezeaux
communes.style_notes: AOC — sweet Chenin Grand Cru. Three steep south-facing slopes. Rich, honeyed, extraordinary aging potential

communes.name: Coteaux de l'Aubance
communes.style_notes: AOC — semi-sweet to sweet Chenin from Aubance valley. Lighter than Layon

communes.name: Saumur
communes.style_notes: AOC — tufa caves, still wines. Red (Cab Franc), white (Chenin), rosé. Clos Rougeard legendary

communes.name: Saumur Mousseux
communes.style_notes: AOC — traditional method sparkling from tufa caves. White and rosé. Bouvet-Ladubay, Gratien & Meyer

communes.name: Saumur-Puy-Notre-Dame
communes.style_notes: AOC — newest Saumur cru (2022). South-facing amphitheatre. Concentrated Cab Franc

communes.name: Rosé de Loire
communes.style_notes: AOC — dry rosé from Anjou, Saumur, or Touraine

communes.name: Anjou Mousseux
communes.style_notes: AOC — sparkling from Anjou. White and rosé

communes.name: Cabernet d'Anjou
communes.style_notes: AOC — semi-sweet rosé from Cabernet. Very popular in France. Off-dry, fruity

communes.name: Rosé d'Anjou
communes.style_notes: AOC — off-dry to sweet rosé. Grolleau-based. Mass-market

communes.name: Anjou-Coteaux de la Loire
communes.style_notes: AOC — semi-sweet to sweet Chenin from west of Angers. Tiny production, near-extinct

communes.name: Coulée de Serrant
communes.style_notes: AOC — monopole of Nicolas Joly. 7ha. Biodynamic icon. One of Loire's greatest dry Chenin. Within Savennières

communes.name: Savennières-Roche aux Moines
communes.style_notes: AOC — south-facing steep slopes within Savennières. Rich, complex, mineral dry Chenin

communes.name: Muscadet Sèvre-et-Maine
communes.style_notes: Crisp mineral white — sur lie aging

communes.name: Muscadet
communes.style_notes: AOC — basic Muscadet from broader zone. Lighter than cru versions

communes.name: Muscadet-Coteaux de la Loire
communes.style_notes: AOC — upstream Loire near Ancenis. Fuller, more structured

communes.name: Muscadet-Côtes de Grandlieu
communes.style_notes: AOC — around Lac de Grandlieu. Lighter, more delicate

communes.name: Muscadet Crus Communaux
communes.style_notes: AOC — 10 named crus: Clisson, Gorges, Le Pallet, Goulaine, Mouzillon-Tillières, Monnières-Saint-Fiacre, Château-Thébaud, La Haye-Fouassière, Vallet, Champtoceaux. Sur lie aging required

communes.name: Gros Plant du Pays Nantais
communes.style_notes: AOC — tart, high-acid Folle Blanche. Seafood wine. Simple but refreshing

communes.name: Coteaux d'Ancenis
communes.style_notes: AOC — near Ancenis. Malvoisie (Pinot Gris) is the specialty — semi-sweet, rich

communes.name: Fiefs Vendéens
communes.style_notes: AOC — Vendée coast. 5 sub-zones: Mareuil, Brem, Vix, Pissotte, Chantonnay. Négrette is the local specialty

communes.name: IGP Val de Loire
communes.style_notes: IGP — entire Loire Valley

wine_regions.name: Champagne
wine_regions.style_notes: World's greatest sparkling wine region

communes.name: Le Mesnil-sur-Oger
communes.style_notes: Blanc de Blancs sparkling

communes.name: Avize
communes.style_notes: Elegant mineral Chardonnay sparkling

communes.name: Cramant
communes.style_notes: Creamy refined Blanc de Blancs

communes.name: Oger
communes.style_notes: Grand Cru — Côte des Blancs. Pure, mineral Chardonnay

communes.name: Chouilly
communes.style_notes: Grand Cru — northernmost Côte des Blancs. Elegant Chardonnay

communes.name: Ambonnay
communes.style_notes: Powerful Pinot-dominant sparkling

communes.name: Bouzy
communes.style_notes: Rich Pinot Noir sparkling and rare still red

communes.name: Verzenay
communes.style_notes: Structured Pinot Noir sparkling

communes.name: Mailly
communes.style_notes: Grand Cru — Montagne de Reims north. Powerful Pinot Noir

communes.name: Verzy
communes.style_notes: Grand Cru — famous for twisted Faux de Verzy beech trees

communes.name: Sillery
communes.style_notes: Grand Cru — historic village, gave its name to 17th-century still Champagne

communes.name: Puisieulx
communes.style_notes: Grand Cru — small village east of Sillery

communes.name: Beaumont-sur-Vesle
communes.style_notes: Grand Cru — north flank of Montagne

communes.name: Louvois
communes.style_notes: Grand Cru — south flank of Montagne de Reims

communes.name: Aÿ
communes.style_notes: Full-bodied Pinot-based sparkling

communes.name: Épernay
communes.style_notes: Headquarters of major Champagne houses

communes.name: Tours-sur-Marne
communes.style_notes: Grand Cru — junction of Montagne de Reims and Marne valley

communes.name: Mareuil-sur-Aÿ
communes.style_notes: Premier Cru — Philipponnat's Clos des Goisses is here

communes.name: Les Riceys
communes.style_notes: AOC — also has its own still rosé AOC (Rosé des Riceys). Largest commune in Champagne by vineyard area

communes.name: Bar-sur-Aube
communes.style_notes: AOC zone — increasingly fashionable. Grower Champagne revolution center. Drappier, Vouette et Sorbée

communes.name: Bar-sur-Seine
communes.style_notes: AOC zone — Pinot Noir country. Cédric Bouchard (Roses de Jeanne) is here

communes.name: Champagne
communes.style_notes: AOC — the appellation itself. 34,000ha, ~300 million bottles/year. 17 Grand Cru villages, 42 Premier Cru

communes.name: Rosé des Riceys
communes.style_notes: AOC — still rosé, not sparkling. Tiny production from Les Riceys. Saignée method. Dark pink, complex

communes.name: Coteaux Champenois
communes.style_notes: AOC — still wines of Champagne. Red (Bouzy Rouge is famous), white, rosé. Rare, cult following

communes.name: IGP Coteaux de Coiffy
communes.style_notes: IGP — Haute-Marne still wines

wine_regions.name: Alsace
wine_regions.style_notes: Aromatic dry and sweet whites

communes.name: Alsace AOC
authorized_grapes: Muscat d'Alsace (Muscat Blanc à Petits Grains)
communes.style_notes: AOC — varietal wines labeled by grape. 13 terroir denominations (Bergheim, Blienschwiller, Côtes de Barr, Côte de Rouffach, Klevener de Heiligenstein, Ottrott, Rodern, Saint-Hippolyte, Scherwiller, Vallée Noble, Val Saint-Grégoire, Wolxheim). Dry by default

communes.name: Alsace Grand Cru
authorized_grapes: Pinot Noir (Hengst & Kirchberg de Barr since 2022)
communes.style_notes: AOC Grand Cru — 51 named vineyards. Noble varieties only (Riesling, Gewurz, Pinot Gris, Muscat + exceptions). Each Grand Cru has unique terroir. Top: Rangen, Schlossberg, Brand, Hengst, Sommerberg, Muenchberg

communes.name: Crémant d'Alsace
communes.style_notes: AOC — France's #1 Crémant by volume. Traditional method. Blanc and Rosé (Pinot Noir). Excellent value sparkling

communes.name: Vendange Tardive (VT)
communes.style_notes: AOC designation — late harvest. Higher must weight required. Off-dry to sweet. No chaptalization. Noble varieties only

communes.name: Sélection de Grains Nobles (SGN)
communes.style_notes: AOC designation — botrytis-affected berries selected individually. Intensely sweet, rich, honeyed. Rarest Alsatian wines

communes.name: Schlossberg
communes.style_notes: Grand Cru — first Alsace GC (1975). Kaysersberg. Pure granite = mineral, steely Riesling. Weinbach benchmark

communes.name: Rangen
communes.style_notes: Grand Cru — Thann. Southernmost and steepest GC. Volcanic soil. Smoky, intense. Zind-Humbrecht is icon

communes.name: Brand
communes.style_notes: Grand Cru — Turckheim. Warm microclimate, south-facing. Rich, exotic, powerful

communes.name: Hengst
communes.style_notes: Grand Cru — Wintzenheim. 'Stallion'. Rich, powerful wines. Josmeyer, Zind-Humbrecht. First GC to allow Pinot Noir

communes.name: Sommerberg
communes.style_notes: Grand Cru — Niedermorschwihr. Steep granite. Albert Boxler's legendary Rieslings

communes.name: Muenchberg
communes.style_notes: Grand Cru — Nothalten. Ostertag's biodynamic icon. Mineral, complex

communes.name: Furstentum
communes.style_notes: Grand Cru — Kientzheim/Sigolsheim. Rich, concentrated. Weinbach, Paul Blanck

communes.name: Mambourg
communes.style_notes: Grand Cru — Sigolsheim. South-facing, warm. Opulent Gewurztraminer. Marcel Deiss

communes.name: Kaefferkopf
communes.style_notes: Grand Cru — Ammerschwihr. 51st and last GC (2007). Unique: allows blends. Mixed geology

communes.name: Zotzenberg
communes.style_notes: Grand Cru — Mittelbergheim. Only GC allowing Sylvaner. Marl-limestone gives rich, mineral style

communes.name: Altenberg de Bergheim
communes.style_notes: Grand Cru — Bergheim. Marcel Deiss's terroir philosophy. Allows field blends (complantation)

communes.name: Kirchberg de Barr
communes.style_notes: Grand Cru — Barr. Second GC to allow Pinot Noir

wine_regions.name: Languedoc-Roussillon
wine_regions.style_notes: France's largest wine region — value and quality

communes.name: Languedoc
communes.style_notes: AOC — mega-appellation from Nîmes to Narbonne. Red, white, rosé. 36 terroir denominations

communes.name: Pic Saint-Loup
communes.style_notes: AOC — elevated to own AOC 2017. Mountain (658m) landmark. Cooler climate. Structured, elegant reds and rosé. Mas Bruguière, Ermitage du Pic Saint-Loup

communes.name: La Clape
communes.style_notes: AOC — former island, now coastal massif near Narbonne. Elevated to AOC 2015. Bourboulenc whites are unique. Château Capitoul, Gérard Bertrand

communes.name: Terrasses du Larzac
communes.style_notes: AOC — elevated 2014. High-altitude (up to 400m) Larzac plateau. Cooler nights = freshness. Mas Jullien, Mas de Daumas Gassac nearby. Star of Languedoc

communes.name: Grès de Montpellier
communes.style_notes: AOC — pebbly/gravelly soils north of Montpellier. Red only. Rich, warm

communes.name: Pézenas
communes.style_notes: AOC — volcanic basalt flows near Pézenas. Red only. Structured, mineral

communes.name: Sommières
communes.style_notes: AOC — newest Languedoc denomination (2011). East of Montpellier

communes.name: Quatourze
communes.style_notes: AOC — near Narbonne. Red only

communes.name: Cabrières
communes.style_notes: AOC — famous for rosé (Clairette rosé tradition). Schist terroir

communes.name: Saint-Saturnin
communes.style_notes: AOC — near Terrasses du Larzac. Red and rosé

communes.name: Montpeyroux
communes.style_notes: AOC — altitude terroir next to Terrasses du Larzac. Concentrated, structured reds

communes.name: Saint-Georges-d'Orques
communes.style_notes: AOC — west of Montpellier. One of oldest Languedoc terroirs

communes.name: Saint-Drézéry
communes.style_notes: AOC — east of Montpellier

communes.name: Saint-Christol
communes.style_notes: AOC — east of Montpellier

communes.name: La Méjanelle
communes.style_notes: AOC — east of Montpellier. Galets roulés like Châteauneuf

communes.name: Minervois
communes.style_notes: AOC — north side of Aude. Large, diverse appellation. Best from La Livinière sub-zone. Structured reds, improving whites

communes.name: Minervois-La Livinière
communes.style_notes: AOC — first Languedoc cru (1999). Red only. Higher altitude, limestone. Concentrated, complex

communes.name: Corbières
communes.style_notes: AOC — massive appellation. 11 terroirs. Garrigue-scented, rustic to refined. Boutenac is the cru

communes.name: Corbières-Boutenac
communes.style_notes: AOC — Corbières cru (2005). Carignan must be included. Schist/clay terroir. Rich, age-worthy

communes.name: Faugères
communes.style_notes: AOC — 100% schist terroir. Mineral, elegant reds and whites. Alain Chabanon, Mas d'Alezon

communes.name: Saint-Chinian
communes.style_notes: AOC — two terroirs: schist north (Berlou, Roquebrun) and limestone south. Spicy, herbal reds

communes.name: Saint-Chinian Berlou
communes.style_notes: AOC — schist sub-zone. Red only. Structured, mineral

communes.name: Saint-Chinian Roquebrun
communes.style_notes: AOC — schist sub-zone. Red only

communes.name: Fitou
communes.style_notes: AOC — first Languedoc AOC (1948). Red only. Two zones: maritime and montagneux. Powerful, dark reds

communes.name: Limoux
communes.style_notes: AOC — still wines: white (Chardonnay-dominated, oak-aged) and red (Merlot-based). High-altitude (300m+)

communes.name: Blanquette de Limoux
communes.style_notes: AOC — traditional method sparkling, predates Champagne (1531 claim). Mauzac gives apple, quince character

communes.name: Blanquette Méthode Ancestrale
communes.style_notes: AOC — original sparkling method. 100% Mauzac, single fermentation. Sweet, gently fizzy, apple-scented

communes.name: Crémant de Limoux
communes.style_notes: AOC — traditional method sparkling, higher Chardonnay/Chenin. Fine, crisp, Champagne-like

communes.name: Picpoul de Pinet
communes.style_notes: AOC — the 'Muscadet of the south'. Zesty, saline white, perfect with oysters from nearby Bassin de Thau

communes.name: Clairette du Languedoc
communes.style_notes: AOC — monovarietal Clairette. Dry and rancio styles. Rare but interesting. Adissan is the heart

communes.name: Muscat de Frontignan
communes.style_notes: AOC VDN — fortified sweet Muscat. One of the oldest French AOCs. Golden, grapey, floral

communes.name: Muscat de Lunel
communes.style_notes: AOC VDN — sweet Muscat from Lunel, between Montpellier and Nîmes

communes.name: Muscat de Mireval
communes.style_notes: AOC VDN — between Frontignan and Montpellier. Lighter than Frontignan

communes.name: Muscat de Saint-Jean-de-Minervois
communes.style_notes: AOC VDN — highest altitude Muscat VDN. Limestone plateau, cooler. More refined, mineral

communes.name: Côtes du Roussillon
communes.style_notes: AOC — broad Roussillon appellation. Red, white, rosé. Improving dramatically

communes.name: Côtes du Roussillon Villages
communes.style_notes: AOC — reds only from 32 superior villages. 4 named crus: Caramany, Latour-de-France, Lesquerde, Tautavel

communes.name: Collioure
communes.style_notes: AOC — dry wines from Banyuls zone. Steep terraced schist facing the sea. Red, white, rosé. Domaine de la Rectorie, Coume del Mas

communes.name: Banyuls
communes.style_notes: AOC VDN — fortified sweet. Rimage (vintage) or oxidative/rancio styles. Like Port but Grenache. Dramatic coastal terraces

communes.name: Banyuls Grand Cru
communes.style_notes: AOC VDN — higher Grenache minimum, longer aging. 30 months in barrel. Rich, complex, rancio capable

communes.name: Maury
communes.style_notes: AOC — both VDN (fortified) and Sec (dry table wine since 2011). Black schist terroir. Mas Amiel is benchmark

communes.name: Rivesaltes
communes.style_notes: AOC VDN — enormous VDN zone across Roussillon. Multiple styles: Ambré, Tuilé, Grenat, Hors d'Âge, Rancio. Extraordinary old wines

communes.name: Muscat de Rivesaltes
communes.style_notes: AOC VDN — sweet Muscat, the most popular French VDN. Grapey, fresh, floral

communes.name: Grand Roussillon
communes.style_notes: AOC VDN — rarely used catch-all VDN for Roussillon

communes.name: IGP Pays d'Oc
communes.style_notes: IGP — France's largest IGP. Incredible value varietals

communes.name: IGP Pays d'Hérault
communes.style_notes: IGP — Mas de Daumas Gassac is here

communes.name: IGP Côtes Catalanes
communes.style_notes: IGP — Roussillon's IGP. Gauby, Matassa

communes.name: IGP Cité de Carcassonne
communes.style_notes: IGP — around Carcassonne

communes.name: IGP Aude
communes.style_notes: IGP — Aude department

communes.name: IGP Gard
communes.style_notes: IGP — Gard department

communes.name: IGP Côtes de Thongue
communes.style_notes: IGP — Béziers/Pézenas. Good value

communes.name: IGP Haute Vallée de l'Aude
communes.style_notes: IGP — Limoux area, high altitude

wine_regions.name: Provence
wine_regions.style_notes: France's rosé capital — also serious reds

communes.name: Côtes de Provence
communes.style_notes: AOC — 80% rosé. France's rosé capital. 4 named sub-zones: Sainte-Victoire, Fréjus, La Londe, Pierrefeu. Whispering Angel put Provence rosé on the map

communes.name: Côtes de Provence Sainte-Victoire
communes.style_notes: AOC — sub-zone east of Aix. Cézanne's mountain. Cooler, more structured

communes.name: Côtes de Provence Fréjus
communes.style_notes: AOC — volcanic soils near coast. Red and rosé

communes.name: Côtes de Provence La Londe
communes.style_notes: AOC — schist terroir near coast. Red and rosé. Mineral, saline

communes.name: Côtes de Provence Notre-Dame des Anges
communes.style_notes: AOC — newest sub-zone (2019). Inland, cooler

communes.name: Bandol
communes.style_notes: AOC — Mourvèdre is king. Powerful, tannic, age-worthy reds (18 months barrel minimum). Domaine Tempier is the icon. Rosé also excellent

communes.name: Cassis
communes.style_notes: AOC — famous for whites (75% production). Dramatic calanque setting. Bouillabaisse wine. Clos Sainte Magdeleine

communes.name: Bellet
communes.style_notes: AOC — tiny (50ha) above Nice. Indigenous varieties. Urban appellation, extreme rarity. Château de Bellet

communes.name: Palette
communes.style_notes: AOC — tiny (50ha) near Aix. 25+ authorized grapes. Château Simone is the monopole effectively

communes.name: Coteaux d'Aix-en-Provence
communes.style_notes: AOC — around Aix. Red, white, rosé. Trévallon (declassified to IGP for Cab Sauv content) is the icon estate

communes.name: Les Baux-de-Provence
communes.style_notes: AOC — Alpilles mountains. Red and rosé. Must be organic since 2019 (first French AOC to mandate). Trévallon, Mas de la Dame

communes.name: Coteaux Varois en Provence
communes.style_notes: AOC — inland Var department. Higher altitude. Red, white, rosé. Good value

communes.name: Pierrevert
communes.style_notes: AOC — highest Provence appellation, near Manosque. Red, white, rosé. Small, obscure

communes.name: IGP Bouches-du-Rhône
communes.style_notes: IGP — Trévallon uses this (too much Cab Sauv for AOC)

communes.name: IGP Var
communes.style_notes: IGP — Var department rosé country

communes.name: IGP Maures
communes.style_notes: IGP — Massif des Maures

communes.name: IGP Alpilles
communes.style_notes: IGP — Les Baux area alternative

wine_regions.name: Jura
wine_regions.style_notes: Unique oxidative wines, vin jaune, and natural wine hub

communes.name: Arbois
communes.style_notes: AOC — Jura's largest and most diverse AOC. All styles: red, white, rosé, vin jaune, vin de paille. Pasteur's hometown. Tissot, Puffeney

communes.name: Arbois-Pupillin
communes.style_notes: AOC — sub-zone of Arbois. 'Capital of Poulsard'. Pierre Overnoy's legendary domaine. Natural wine mecca

communes.name: Château-Chalon
communes.style_notes: AOC — Vin Jaune only. 100% Savagnin aged 6 years+ under voile (yeast film) in 620ml clavelin bottles. Sherry-like but unfortified. Walnut, curry, extreme complexity. One of world's most unique wines

communes.name: L'Étoile
communes.style_notes: AOC — white wines only. Named for star-shaped fossils. Vin jaune, Crémant, and still white. Domaine de Montbourgeau

communes.name: Côtes du Jura
communes.style_notes: AOC — regional Jura appellation. All styles. Great producers: Jean-François Ganevat, Domaine Labet

communes.name: Crémant du Jura
communes.style_notes: AOC — traditional method sparkling. Excellent quality. Blanc and Rosé. Growing reputation

communes.name: Macvin du Jura
communes.style_notes: AOC — mistelle (grape must + marc spirit). Sweet, aperitif wine. Red and white. Unique to Jura

communes.name: IGP Franche-Comté
communes.style_notes: IGP — covers Jura and surrounds

wine_regions.name: Southwest France
wine_regions.style_notes: Indigenous grapes, value wines

communes.name: Bergerac
communes.style_notes: AOC — 'Bordeaux's backyard'. Red, white (dry and sweet), rosé. Good value Bordeaux-style blends

communes.name: Pécharmant
communes.style_notes: AOC — Bergerac's best red zone. Iron-rich tran soils. More structured than basic Bergerac

communes.name: Montravel
communes.style_notes: AOC — western Bergerac. Red and dry white. Haut-Montravel and Côtes de Montravel for sweet whites

communes.name: Monbazillac
communes.style_notes: AOC — botrytized sweet white, 'poor man's Sauternes'. North-facing slopes over Dordogne = morning mist. Excellent value sweet wine

communes.name: Saussignac
communes.style_notes: AOC — sweet white near Monbazillac. Must be botrytis-affected

communes.name: Rosette
communes.style_notes: AOC — semi-sweet white north of Bergerac. Nearly extinct

communes.name: Cahors
communes.style_notes: AOC — the 'Black Wine'. Malbec's original home. Causse (plateau) vs. terraces give different styles. Mas del Périé, Clos Triguedina

communes.name: Buzet
communes.style_notes: AOC — Bordeaux-style blends from Lot-et-Garonne. Co-op dominated. Good value

communes.name: Côtes du Marmandais
communes.style_notes: AOC — Abouriou is the indigenous specialty grape. Bordeaux-style otherwise

communes.name: Côtes de Duras
communes.style_notes: AOC — east of Bordeaux. Bordeaux-style reds and crisp Sauvignon whites

communes.name: Brulhois
communes.style_notes: AOC — between Agen and Moissac. Red and rosé. Tannat required

communes.name: Madiran
communes.style_notes: AOC — Tannat is king. Massively tannic, dark, powerful. Alain Brumont (Montus/Bouscassé) pioneered modern style. Needs aging

communes.name: Pacherenc du Vic-Bilh
communes.style_notes: AOC — same zone as Madiran but whites. Dry (Sec) and sweet (moelleux). Petit Manseng is the star. Rare, indigenous

communes.name: Jurançon
communes.style_notes: AOC — Pau foothills. Sweet (moelleux) from passerillage (drying on vine). Henry IV baptized with Jurançon. Extraordinary aromatics: tropical, honey, spice

communes.name: Jurançon Sec
communes.style_notes: AOC — dry version. Gros Manseng dominant. Crisp, aromatic, citrus, stone fruit. Clos Uroulat, Camin Larredya

communes.name: Irouléguy
communes.style_notes: AOC — Basque country, Pyrenees mountains. Heroic terraced viticulture. Red, white, rosé. Basque culture. Domaine Arretxea, Brana

communes.name: Béarn
communes.style_notes: AOC — broad Béarn area. Red, white, rosé. Light wines, mostly rosé. Bellocq sub-zone

communes.name: Saint-Mont
communes.style_notes: AOC — next to Madiran. Red, white, rosé. Plaimont co-op dominates. Pre-phylloxera vines preserved

communes.name: Tursan
communes.style_notes: AOC — Landes department. Baroque is the indigenous white grape. Michel Guérard (chef) is a major producer

communes.name: Fronton
communes.style_notes: AOC — Toulouse's wine. Négrette is unique to Fronton. Violet-scented, peppery, light to medium

communes.name: Gaillac
communes.style_notes: AOC — ancient vineyard (Gallo-Roman). Indigenous grapes: Duras, Braucol, Mauzac, Len de l'El, Prunelard, Ondenc. Dry, sweet, sparkling. Méthode Gaillacoise (ancestral) sparkling is traditional. Plageoles is the heritage guardian

communes.name: Gaillac Premières Côtes
communes.style_notes: AOC — red only from best hillside sites. Richer, more structured

communes.name: Marcillac
communes.style_notes: AOC — Aveyron gorges. Fer Servadou on iron-rich soils. Rustic, peppery, wild herb character. Red and rosé

communes.name: Côtes du Lot (Entraygues-et-du-Fel)
communes.style_notes: AOC — extreme Aveyron mountain viticulture. Tiny production

communes.name: Estaing
communes.style_notes: AOC — tiny Aveyron AOC. Mountain wines, heroic viticulture

communes.name: Côtes de Millau
communes.style_notes: AOC — near the famous viaduct. Light reds and rosés, mostly Gamay

communes.name: IGP Côtes de Gascogne
communes.style_notes: IGP — France's best white IGP. Crisp Colombard blends. Tariquet

communes.name: IGP Comté Tolosan
communes.style_notes: IGP — broad Southwest umbrella

communes.name: IGP Côtes du Tarn
communes.style_notes: IGP — Tarn department

communes.name: IGP Côtes du Lot
communes.style_notes: IGP — Lot department, Cahors area

wine_regions.name: Savoie
wine_regions.style_notes: Alpine wines — crisp whites and peppery reds

communes.name: Vin de Savoie
communes.style_notes: AOC — 20 named crus can append name: Apremont, Abymes, Chignin, Chignin-Bergeron, Arbin, Cruet, Jongieux, Marignan, Marin, Ripaille, Crépy, Ayze, etc. Mountain wines, crisp, mineral

communes.name: Vin de Savoie Apremont
communes.style_notes: AOC Cru — largest Savoie cru. 1248 landslide debris. Crisp, mineral Jacquère with slight pétillance

communes.name: Vin de Savoie Abymes
